title: Our Home
description:
For the first time since getting engaged, they browsed Gangnam listings together.

Scrolling past a three-bedroom, Daeun's hand stopped.
"This room... how about it for your father?"
{name} froze. He'd never even thought of it.
"And this side, for when my mom comes up to Seoul."

The three billion that had been 'my deed' for five years became something else with that one sentence.
A number he'd climbed alone — was now a home with several rooms.

choices.text: "Yeah. Let's find one with a room for both of them."
choices.result_text:
Daeun beamed.

That night, for the first time, {name} thought of Gangnam not as 'where I arrive' but 'where we live.'
The weight of the number changed. Heavier now — and yet, strangely, lighter.

choices.text: "Let's think about that after we get in. Right now the number comes first."
choices.result_text:
Daeun went quiet for a moment, then closed the screen.
"...Right. The number comes first."

{name} felt the temperature of her voice drop half a degree, but his head was already back in the listing math.
How many rooms it had — was a problem for later.

description_if_known.father_passed:
For the first time since getting engaged, they browsed Gangnam listings together.

Scrolling past a three-bedroom, Daeun's hand stopped.
"Let's keep this room for your father. Hang a photo of him."
{name} froze. His father was gone now — but Daeun wanted to leave a place for him.

"And this side, for when my mom comes up to Seoul."

The three billion that had been 'my deed' for five years became something else.
A number he'd climbed alone — was now a home with a place for both the departed and the living.

title: The Families Meet
description:
The introductions. A quiet Korean restaurant.

{name}'s father — a lifetime in the factory, stooped shoulders, a borrowed suit. Daeun's mother — up on the dawn bus from the countryside, knuckles thick from work.

Neither of them had anything. You could see it at a glance.

His father spoke, with effort.
"I... once did a terrible thing to my child, over a debt. A shameful father..."

Silence settled over the table. Daeun's mother looked at {name}.
Whatever {name} said next — his father's remaining pride hung on it.

choices.text: "My father paid off every won of that debt. Everything I am, I owe to him."
choices.result_text:
His father lifted his head. His eyes were red.

Daeun's mother said quietly, "You've got a good father."

On the way home, his father clapped {name} once on the back.
No words — but that was enough.

choices.text: Change the subject. (The debt talk doesn't belong here)
choices.result_text:
{name} hurried to bring up something else. The venue, the date, the budget.

And so his father's words were buried, trailing off over the table.

On the way home, his father was quieter than usual.
{name} knew what that silence meant, and pretended he didn't.

title: The Shortcut
description:
The deadline was close. One step short of Gangnam.

Sangchul pushed a coffee across the table.
"There is one way. Take out a loan under your in-laws' name, hold the property under your wife's name — and you skip the taxes, the regulations, all of it."

"Your wife doesn't even need to know. Just get her stamp on the papers."

Using his wife as a name on a document. And Gangnam would be in reach.
Sangchul smiled. It was a smile he'd seen somewhere before.

choices.result_text:
Sangchul shrugged. "Well. Your call."

The road home was long. Gangnam drifted a step further away.
And yet, strangely, his steps were light.

{name} understood now why that smile was familiar. Five years ago, that's how someone had smiled while introducing a deal to his father.

choices.text: "...Just her stamp, right." (Borrows his wife's name)
choices.result_text:
Daeun stamped the papers without asking a thing. Because she trusts {name}.

The moment he turned that trust into a document, {name} became Sangchul.
Started out hating him, ended up doing that to his own wife.

Gangnam came a step closer. And something, soundlessly, cracked.

title: The Last Step
description:
One last step to the Gangnam deed.

And that step — could only be reached by betraying Daeun. Liquidate the property he'd quietly held in her name and she loses everything, but {name} stands in Gangnam.

The contract sits in front of him. In the next room, Daeun is picking wedding invitation designs. Humming.

He picked up the pen.

Three billion was in this one signature. And Daeun, too, was in this one signature.

choices.text: Put the pen down. "Daeun, let's just... get there a little later."
choices.result_text:
Daeun came out of the room. "What'd you say?"
"Nothing. Did you pick a pretty invitation?"

The shortcut went in the trash that night.
Gangnam would come honestly, or it wouldn't come at all — one of the two.
Either way, he wasn't trading it for the person humming in the next room.
{name} learned that day it was worth more than any deed.

choices.text: Sign it. Gangnam is one step ahead.
choices.result_text:
He signed. The Gangnam deed came into his hands.

It didn't take Daeun long to learn the truth.
She didn't cry. Like someone who had already, quietly, cried it all out years ago.

"...When did you start seeing me as a document?"

{name} couldn't answer. He couldn't name the exact date.
The seal they'd never put on a marriage registration finally met paper — on the agreement ending their life together.

choices.text: (Pen in hand — that post-it in the drawer came to mind.)
choices.result_text:
Pen still in hand, {name} opened the desk drawer.
One old post-it note. Years had passed since he peeled it off the fridge and put it here.
'Eat properly.' Three words, written careful and round.

The person who wrote these words was in the next room right now, humming, choosing wedding invitation designs.
Selling off everything she had with one secret signature — and these three words — could not exist in the same world.

{name} stuck the post-it onto the contract, and put the pen down.
"Daeun. Let's just... go a little late."
The humming in the next room paused a moment, then went on. Knowing nothing. That was good.

description_if_known.namsan_lock_daeun:
One last step to the Gangnam deed.

And that step — could only be reached by betraying Daeun. Liquidate the property he'd quietly held in her name and she loses everything, but {name} stands in Gangnam.

As he picked up the pen, Namsan came to mind. The padlock fastened to the railing. The night they'd said, come find it in ten years.
That lock would still be there.

In the next room, Daeun is picking wedding invitation designs. Humming.
Three billion was in this one signature. And Daeun, too, was in this one signature.

title: The Wedding Package
description:
Wedding prep. {name} took the estimate in hand and, for a moment, couldn't breathe.

Studio-dress-makeup package: 4.8 million. Hall rental and catering: 18 million. Ye-dan and gifts: 5 million. Honeymoon: 4 million.
Five separate invitation dinners, each one on {name}'s tab.

All told, it was a jeonse deposit's worth. That much comes straight out of the seed money for Gangnam.

Daeun glanced at the estimate and said,
"...Do we really have to do it like this?"

choices.text: "Let's keep it small. Minimal package, put that money toward our home."
choices.result_text:
Daeun smiled, relieved.
"Honestly, spending millions to wear a dress for one day felt like a waste to me too."

A small hall, family and a few close friends. Self-shot photos by the Han River instead of a studio.
It might have looked shabby to others — but every won saved went straight into their future.
Living with someone who values substance over appearance — {name} felt steadier for it.

choices.text: "It's once in a lifetime. Let's do it like everyone else does."
choices.result_text:
They went full package. The dress was beautiful, the photos gorgeous, the guests envious.

After the ceremony, settling the bills, {name} looked at the account. 31 million, gone in a single day.

Daeun said nothing, but they both knew that money would have put Gangnam months closer.
A wedding just like everyone else's. Just like everyone else's — exactly that much.

title: The One Waiting First
description:
The wedding day. The groom's entrance was already over.

{name} had walked the aisle alone and taken his place at the altar. In the few seconds while the MC prepared the next cue, both guest sections lay open before him. Daeun's side was packed with hometown friends, mart coworkers, and relatives. It wasn't one or two gaps on his side. The entire left section looked empty.

For five years, he'd watched charts instead of meeting people and worked overtime instead of going out. At some point, he'd stopped even thinking of names to call with good news.

The music changed. "Please welcome the bride."

The rear doors opened and Daeun appeared. As she stepped slowly onto the aisle, the empty seats and the faces who had come occupied the same frame.

choices.text: Don't avoid the empty groom's chairs. Look all the way down the rows.
choices.result_text:
He had thought that if he didn't look, it might not count. So {name} looked at the chairs one by one.

The seats were empty, but faces came to mind: people whose calls he had put off, people he hadn't met because the numbers came first, people he'd promised to call as one season passed into another.

His breath caught once. He did not look away.

choices.text: Turn to the bride's side and bow first to the people who came today.
choices.result_text:
When {name} gave a short bow, the applause grew a little louder.

A mart coworker who had traded shifts, a hometown friend who had taken the dawn bus, relatives he'd met only once. Every one of them had made time to be here for Daeun.

At the end of the aisle, Daeun saw the greeting and smiled. Only then did {name} understand that this wedding was not something he was doing alone.

description_if_known.father_passed:
The wedding day. The groom's entrance was already over.

{name} had walked the aisle alone and taken his place at the altar. The groom's section on the left was empty. One front-row seat stood out more sharply than the rest. It was where his father should have been.

If only he'd been a little faster, his father could have sat there and seen this. Not even money could move time forward today.

The music changed. "Please welcome the bride."

The rear doors opened and Daeun appeared. As she stepped slowly onto the aisle, his father's empty seat and Daeun occupied the same frame.
description_if_known.father_reconciled:
The wedding day. The groom's entrance was already over.

{name} had walked the aisle alone and taken his place at the altar. The groom's section on the left was sparse. Still, beyond the flowers, he heard his father straighten up — the scrape of an armrest under hands that had worked a factory floor for a lifetime.

Rows of empty chairs or not, his father had come. Today, that was bigger than a hundred guests.

The music changed. "Please welcome the bride."

The rear doors opened and Daeun appeared. As she stepped slowly onto the aisle, his father and Daeun entered the same field of view.
description_if_known.hyunsu_reconnected:
The wedding day. The groom's entrance was already over.

{name} had walked the aisle alone and taken his place at the altar. The groom's section on the left was bare. From beyond the flowers came Hyunsu's voice: "Hyung, look ahead. You'll ruin the photos."

{name} laughed, and his throat tightened. Even one person who knew these five years had come.

The music changed. "Please welcome the bride."

The rear doors opened and Daeun appeared. As she stepped slowly onto the aisle, Hyunsu's voice dissolved into the applause.
description_if_known.daeun_hometown_visited:
The wedding day. The groom's entrance was already over.

{name} had walked the aisle alone and taken his place at the altar. In the front row on the bride's side sat Daeun's mother, up on the dawn bus from the countryside, work-thickened hands on her knees. Just as she had that night at her table, she met {name}'s eyes and gave one silent nod.

The groom's section on the left was sparse. Even so, that one person in the front row reached him before the empty chairs did.

The music changed. "Please welcome the bride."

The rear doors opened and Daeun appeared. Her mother's eyes followed her daughter down the aisle.
description_if_known.namsan_lock_daeun:
The wedding day. The groom's entrance was already over.

{name} had walked the aisle alone and taken his place at the altar. The groom's section on the left was sparse; the right was packed with Daeun's people.

The music changed. "Please welcome the bride."

The rear doors opened and Daeun appeared. In that instant, he remembered the railing on Namsan. "Come find it in ten years." The promise from the night they fastened the padlock was now coming toward {name} down the aisle.

title: At Daeun's Pace
description:
Daeun's first step. The hem of her dress swept the aisle. On the second, a flash went off. On the third, applause and music folded into each other.

Even through the noise, he saw Daeun's lips move.

"Minjun."

She was too far away for him to hear her, but he could recognize his own name. Daeun did not hurry. As she had for five years, she was coming toward {name} at her own pace.

The distance between them shortened one step at a time.

choices.text: As if he heard his name, loosen his rigid shoulders and meet Daeun's eyes.
choices.result_text:
When their eyes met, Daeun's mouth softened.

The applause and camera shutters moved one step farther away. He saw, in order, her hands around the bouquet, the lips pressed together to hold back tears, the smile spreading at the corners of her eyes.

Only a few steps remained. The empty groom's section and the person approaching him now fit in the same view.

title: The Groom's Side
description:
Daeun was halfway down the aisle.

On one side was Daeun coming closer: the person who had passed him triangle gimbap across a convenience-store counter, the person who had fallen asleep on his shoulder in that narrow room on a rainy night.

On the other were the empty chairs. The calls he had put off and the faces he'd lost while chasing Gangnam remained in the shape of neat chair backs.

Behind her bouquet, Daeun quietly formed the words, "It's okay." He couldn't tell whether she meant the empty seats, his shaking hands, or the last five years.

Before Daeun reached the altar, {name}'s gaze stood one last time between the two.

choices.text: Look only at Daeun. The groom's side is empty, but she's coming toward him.
choices.result_text:
Daeun walked down the aisle toward {name}. Instead of the empty seats beside him, {name} watched the person coming closer.

However many guests there were, it didn't matter. One person to spend a life with was enough.
Daeun stopped before the altar. The empty groom's section, strangely, no longer stung.

choices.text: Beyond Daeun approaching him, the empty groom's section stings. What did he run five years for?
choices.result_text:
From the altar, {name}'s eyes kept catching on the empty chairs.

Gangnam had come closer, and along that road people had dropped away one by one.
Only today could he see the tally. What he'd gained, and what he'd lost without even a goodbye.
The short time it took Daeun to reach him felt unusually long.
